sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule and rostrum dark brown to chocolate brown; antennae brown; body yellow-brown; legs pale yellow. Head and body sparsely covered with fine hairs and scattered with a few longer setae. Body length 3.30—3.90 mm. Head pear-shaped, strongly constricted behind the antennae; posterior sides weakly convex; posterior margin concave at the middle; rostrum slightly upturned in lateral view, weakly concave dorsally, with a shallow swelling at the base of the rostrum; head length including rostrum 1.675—1.725 mm, head length excluding rostrum 0.95—0.975 mm, maximum width 0.812—0.862 mm. Frontal gland small, with a fine duct opening at the tip of the rostrum. Rostrum slender, narrow, cylindrical, slightly shorter than the head length excluding the rostrum (length 0.70—0.75 mm, rostrum length/head length index 0.702—0.769). Antennae 12-segmented; segment 2 shortest, segment 3 slender and much longer than segment 2. Mandibles reduced, with obtuse outer margins, sometimes acute apically. Pronotum strongly saddle-shaped; anterior lobe strongly upturned, with a notch at the middle of the anterior margin; posterior margin straight (length 0.187—0.20 mm, maximum width 0.48—0.525 mm). Mesonotum wider than the pronotum, metanotum wider than the mesonotum; posterior margins of both nearly straight.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule yellow-brown to brown; antennae, labrum and body pale yellow. Head moderately hairy, body densely hairy. Body length 3.52—3.85 mm. Head capsule subcircular, sides weakly convex; coronal suture with a median arm; head length to mandible base 0.888—0.925 mm, maximum width 0.95—1.05 mm. Fontanelle plate elongate, translucent white. Antennae 13—14-segmented; segment 3 shortest in the 13-segmented antenna, segment 4 shortest in the 14-segmented antenna. Postclypeus inflated, less than half as long as wide. Pronotum strongly saddle-shaped; length 0.237—0.275 mm, maximum width 0.525—0.575 mm.

note: Adapted from the entry in Chhotani (1997), original in English; the soldier and worker are described, while the alate is recorded as unknown in the original; synonymy list, figure numbers and distribution records are not translated. The species name is frequently mis-OCR'd in the original as "Alnpoulitermes"; the Chinese genus name given to Ampoulitermes is a proposed translation.
